message.reasoning_content:
Key bugs: parse_u64 sets out=0 first, violating "out unchanged on failure" (e.g. "12x" leaves out=0, or overflow "99999999999999999999" wraps). Also overflow: no check against UINT64_MAX; contract says reject above UINT64_MAX — but uint64_t can't represent UINT64_MAX... wait, UINT64_MAX presumably means UINT64_MAX (2^64-1)? "values above UINT64_MAX" — uint64_t max is 2^64-1 = UINT64_MAX. So overflow wraps silently, violating contract. Also empty string accepted (returns true, out=0) — contract says nonempty only. Leading zeros allowed — fine.

Registry: get returns string_view into names vector while holding lock_guard — lock released after return, but the view aliases vector's strings; concurrent add may push_back causing reallocation/remove of elements, invalidating the view (dangling). Also get(i) no bounds check — out-of-range read. Also readers retaining views while add reallocates → dangling reference. Also get returns view to element that add may move. Fix: return std::string (copy) or keep views stable via deque of unique_ptr / chunked storage; bounds check.

Also parse_u64 noexcept but overflow check fine. Also out=0 on failure violates unchanged-on-failure.

Minimal triggers:
1. parse_u64("12x", out) with out=5 → returns false but out becomes 0 (violates unchanged).
2. parse_u64("") → returns true (accepts empty, contract says nonempty).
3. parse_u64("18446744073789591616"?) overflow: "99999999999999999999" wraps → returns true garbage.
4. Registry.get with i >= names.size() → out-of-bounds read (UB).
5. Reader retains view from get, writer add triggers vector reallocation → dangling view (UB read).
Also get holds lock_guard then returns view — fine lock-wise, but the aliasing issue.

Fixes: parse_u64: check empty, accumulate with overflow check (out > (UINT64_MAX - d)/10), only assign out at end on success; leave out untouched on failure. Registry: bounds check; return std::string by value or store views stably (e.g., std::vector<std::unique_ptr<std::string>> or deque chunks) so add never invalidates.

Corrected parse_u64 in cpp block. Keep ≤650 words, ≤6 findings.
